title: Custom modules
idea: A custom module is a file of your own that exports a few functions and keeps the rest private.
points: Give each module one job: the model, `book.model.js`, holds the books and nothing else.
Callers import the whole API with `import * as Book from './book.model.js'`.
Return copies, so a caller cannot edit stored objects by accident.
Node loads a module once, so every importer shares the same store.

steps.caption: Inside `book.model.js`, `books` and `nextId` sit in the module's own scope. Nothing outside can name them.
Five `export` lines form the public API: `findAll`, `findById`, `create`, `update` and `remove`.
Another file imports those functions and calls them. It never touches the data directly.
Only the exported functions read and change the private state.
Asking for `books` by name finds nothing: `Book.books` is `undefined`, and `import { books }` is a SyntaxError.

code.title: The module
code.caption: The Book Store data as its own module. In the project it lives at `src/models/book.model.js`.

walk.text: These two names are not exported, so no other file can reach them.
`findAll` returns copies, so a caller cannot edit the stored books.
`findById` returns a copy, or `undefined` when no book has that id.
`create` keeps only the three named fields and assigns the next id.
`update` replaces a book; `undefined` means no such id.
`remove` answers `true` or `false`. The model never sends HTTP replies.

code.title: Using the module
code.caption: A script beside the module imports it. From `src/controllers/`, the path would be `../models/book.model.js`.

pitfalls: Do not export the `books` array: any importer could push to it or splice items out.
Avoid circular imports, where two files import each other: an export may not be ready.
Do not send HTTP replies from the model: return `undefined` and let the caller pick `404`.

quiz.why: `findById` returns a copy, so editing it leaves the stored year at 1984. `remove(1)` leaves two books.

takeaway: Export behavior, not data: callers get functions, never the array.

starters: Should I use named exports or `export default`?
Why does the model return copies of the books?
How do I import a file from a parent folder?
